title: A workout that will not delete says try again but keeps no note of why
what: When the member deletes a saved workout and the delete fails, the page says 'Could not delete this workout. It is still here. Please try again.' The real error is thrown away before that message, so not even the phone's own log says why. Repeat, Edit and Save as routine all write their error first; Delete does not.
expected: Every failed delete writes the reason to the phone log before the calm message, like the other workout actions.
fix_line: Write the error to the log in the delete's failure path before saying try again.

title: The exercise library update can fail at every app start, or after a restore, with no trace
what: On app start, and after a backup restore or an undo, the app links the member's old exercises to the built-in library and adds new exercises. If that fails, the error is thrown away with no log line and no word on screen. It retries on the next start, so a fault that repeats leaves the member's exercises without library pictures, muscles or new entries for good, and nobody can see why. The earlier finding covered the demo-data re-link only.
expected: A failed library update writes its reason to the phone log each time, so a repeating failure can be found.
how_often: rare, after an app update or a restore
fix_line: Log the error at the three places that start the library update instead of discarding it.

items.reason: backups and restores live in the backup and cloud code; this area only re-links the library after a restore (see L6.6)
no scheduled jobs in this area; the library update runs on app start
this area holds no clock, timer, heart-rate or watch code; the In use words are handed the seconds left by the rest clock elsewhere
